name: TC-UX PLAN: dependency-safe start and truthful task detail
prompt:
Product Contract: TC-UX v1.0
Objective: make AgentOS task-chain execution dependency-safe and make task detail pages show only truthful, resource-scoped prompt, output, activity, and control state.

Approved product behavior:
1. Normal task-chain execution is sequential. A chain step may be started manually only when every earlier surviving chain step is DONE, the target is the next executable AGENT step, it is TODO or BACKLOG, it has no active run, its assignee/repo are valid, and its run budget remains. This preserves recovery of the current parked BACKLOG step and a genuinely stalled next step. V1 provides no force-bypass action.
2. The API, not only the button, enforces the dependency rule under an explicit concurrency/locking design. Starting step N while any earlier step is TODO, BACKLOG, DOING, or REVIEW returns a specific 409 and creates no Run or activity claim. Non-chain manual start remains supported.
3. Navigating between task ids must never render or mutate using another task's stale data. A path change immediately invalidates actionable resource state; loading, 404, and transient-error behavior are explicit. Missing step output renders an honest empty state and can never retain a prior task's artifact. Task-scoped drafts, expansion state, errors, and actions reset or are keyed to task identity.
4. The prompt card leads with the unique step or human responsibility, separates/collapses the common Product Contract, calls itself the task prompt, and explains that the effective runner prompt also includes foundational prompt, role prompt, tool manifest, and available prior outputs. It must not claim to render content it does not have.
5. Chain UI distinguishes the task being viewed from the chain step actually executing. Use truthful labels such as Viewed here versus Current execution, label progress as Completed n/m, show an explicit no-output state, and render HUMAN with a human glyph rather than the robot Agent chip.
6. Start/recovery actions state their effect. The normal row action is shown only on the dependency-safe next step; no future-step Start now controls. If the valid step is parked, label it as recovery. Errors name the blocking predecessor.
7. Active dispatched chain gates are immutable through ordinary Task PATCH/UI. Chain status changes cannot mark a future step DONE ahead of unfinished predecessors or mark a task DONE while it has an active run. The detail page must not present unrestricted controls that contradict these guards. Legitimate Inbox gate decisions, retry, parking, unarchive, and automatic advancement remain supported.

In scope: apps/web task detail, chain list, shared polling/resource identity behavior and focused state reset; API chain rendering/startability and POST start guard; necessary workflow/locking helpers; API/UI status and approval-gate guards; localized copy; human chip/presentation; unit, integration, DB concurrency, and browser regression tests; documentation/spec errata needed to replace the old intentional out-of-order behavior.
Out of scope: new general template authoring UI; new runtime router; production activation or restart; database migrations unless a reviewed plan proves unavoidable; changing runner model selection; unrelated board redesign; a force-start override; changes to CP-A workspace-root ownership behavior.

Acceptance and required evidence:
A1. Reproduce step 3 output followed by a no-output step: the destination title/prompt/status are correct, the output card says no output recorded, and revised-plan text is absent after both settled and immediate navigation states.
A2. Automated path-switch tests prove no stale task can be patched, archived, started, or commented through destination actions; activity drafts and local detail state do not cross task ids.
A3. The seven TC-UX prompts visibly expose different step responsibilities without expanding the common contract; the UI truthfully describes the effective-prompt components.
A4. With steps 1-3 DONE and step 4 DOING, steps 5+ expose no start action. Direct POST start for 5 or 6 returns 409, names the unfinished predecessor, creates zero Runs, and leaves all statuses/output/activity unchanged.
A5. With predecessors DONE and the next step TODO, one manual start succeeds exactly once; with that step BACKLOG it moves to TODO and queues exactly once. Double-start and completion/start races remain idempotent.
A6. A REVIEW approval gate blocks every successor. HUMAN never has a robot glyph or start action. Viewed here and Current execution cannot point to the same semantic marker unless they are actually the same row.
A7. PATCH cannot mutate approvalGate on a dispatched chain; cannot complete a future chain step; cannot complete an active-run task. Inbox approval and automatic successor activation still pass existing tests.
A8. Focused web tests, API unit tests, real DB tests using only the dedicated test database, typecheck, build, full affected tests, git diff check, and browser verification pass on one final rebased tree.
A9. One shared branch and one PR contain the plan/review/implementation history. Final evidence records exact base/head, checks, changed symbols, and any accepted limitations. No production command, restart, migration, or live task mutation is used as a test.

Risks and stopping conditions: Critical task-routing, concurrency, idempotency, gate authority, and cross-resource mutation risk. Stop on an unexplained Run creation, any mutation of the live CP-A chain, need to weaken a gate or dependency, evidence that current master does not reproduce the reported bug, need for migration, overlapping ownership of the same exact branch/worktree, or any required production restart. Use scratch fixtures and the existing dedicated test database only; never press current live future-step controls as a test.
Dependencies and prerequisites: work in an isolated AgentOS run workspace and shared chain branch based on freshly fetched current master. The live diagnosis was observed on checkout a5fb926, while origin/master was 70995b5 at dispatch; re-verify and record current authority before implementation and again before final review. CP-A may continue independently; avoid its ownership/startup symbols and stop for a real semantic conflict. The local codex/review-role-convergence branch is not this chain's write surface.

Routing Contract: v1.0
Route: Planned Critical
Implementation Agent: senior-dev
Reason: the fix changes chain dependency enforcement, status/gate authority, concurrent Run creation, and cross-task mutation safety. These are Critical even though part of the symptom is frontend UI.
SPEC decision: no SPEC step; Leo approved the intended product behavior and removal of ordinary out-of-order start on 2026-08-17. A written reviewed Plan is still required for locking, state identity, sequencing, rollback, and regression evidence.

Step responsibility: inspect current master and live evidence read-only. Persist an English implementation plan under docs/plans/ covering resource-identity polling, missing-output semantics, component key/reset boundaries, API chain predecessor checks and lock ordering, status/gate guards, localized UX, test seams, rollout and rollback. Reconcile the old spec that intentionally allowed out-of-order start with this approved Product Contract; the Product Contract wins. Do not implement product code.

Objective: make AgentOS task-chain execution dependency-safe and make task detail pages show only truthful, resource-scoped prompt, output, activity, and control state.

Approved product behavior:
1. Normal task-chain execution is sequential. A chain step may be started manually only when every earlier surviving chain step is DONE, the target is the next executable AGENT step, it is TODO or BACKLOG, it has no active run, its assignee/repo are valid, and its run budget remains. This preserves recovery of the current parked BACKLOG step and a genuinely stalled next step. V1 provides no force-bypass action.
2. The API, not only the button, enforces the dependency rule under an explicit concurrency/locking design. Starting step N while any earlier step is TODO, BACKLOG, DOING, or REVIEW returns a specific 409 and creates no Run or activity claim. Non-chain manual start remains supported.
3. Navigating between task ids must never render or mutate using another task's stale data. A path change immediately invalidates actionable resource state; loading, 404, and transient-error behavior are explicit. Missing step output renders an honest empty state and can never retain a prior task's artifact. Task-scoped drafts, expansion state, errors, and actions reset or are keyed to task identity.
4. The prompt card leads with the unique step or human responsibility, separates/collapses the common Product Contract, calls itself the task prompt, and explains that the effective runner prompt also includes foundational prompt, role prompt, tool manifest, and available prior outputs. It must not claim to render content it does not have.
5. Chain UI distinguishes the task being viewed from the chain step actually executing. Use truthful labels such as Viewed here versus Current execution, label progress as Completed n/m, show an explicit no-output state, and render HUMAN with a human glyph rather than the robot Agent chip.
6. Start/recovery actions state their effect. The normal row action is shown only on the dependency-safe next step; no future-step Start now controls. If the valid step is parked, label it as recovery. Errors name the blocking predecessor.
7. Active dispatched chain gates are immutable through ordinary Task PATCH/UI. Chain status changes cannot mark a future step DONE ahead of unfinished predecessors or mark a task DONE while it has an active run. The detail page must not present unrestricted controls that contradict these guards. Legitimate Inbox gate decisions, retry, parking, unarchive, and automatic advancement remain supported.

A5. With predecessors DONE and the next step TODO, one manual start succeeds exactly once; with that step BACKLOG it moves to TODO and queues exactly once. Double-start and completion/start races remain idempotent.
A6. A REVIEW approval gate blocks every successor. HUMAN never has a robot glyph or start action. Viewed here and Current execution cannot point to the same semantic marker unless they are actually the same row.
A7. PATCH cannot mutate approvalGate on a dispatched chain; cannot complete a future chain step; cannot complete an active-run task. Inbox approval and automatic successor activation still pass existing tests.
